quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: Why should you keep a safe distance behind other vehicles?

options.text: To give yourself time and space to see and react to dangers ahead.
So you can follow the car in front of you closely.
To help traffic counters count you as a vehicle.
To encourage other drivers to cut in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: To give yourself time and space to see and react to dangers ahead.
questions.explanation: A safe distance gives you space to stop or move if the car ahead stops suddenly. It also helps you see hazards on the road, like potholes.

questions.question: When you are stopped, what gear should you be in?
questions.correctAnswerText: First gear.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow down or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, what should you NOT do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Brake suddenly.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes gently. Do not brake suddenly.

questions.question: When stopping, how should you apply the brakes?

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time.
Use only one brake, front or rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Apply them together at the same time.

questions.question: How should a group of riders pass another vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, riders should pass one at a time. The second rider waits until the first rider is safely back in the original lane before passing. This pattern continues until all riders have passed.

questions.question: What does it mean when a rider extends their left arm straight out to the left?

options.text: The rider plans to turn left.
The rider is about to stop.
The rider plans to turn right.
The rider is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider plans to turn left.
questions.explanation: Riders use hand signals instead of turn signals to show their intent. A left arm extended straight out means the rider plans to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: The driver will definitely yield to you.
It does not mean the driver will yield to you.
The driver knows you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean the driver will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that eye contact means another driver will give you the right-of-way. Always drive defensively.

questions.question: Which type of sign is rectangular?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs that post rules, like speed limits, are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your entire face and eyes.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not enough protection.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's braking power comes from the front brake?
questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least three-quarters of the motorcycle's stopping power.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Ride at a slower speed than usual.
Stay closer to the car in front of you.
Ride at a faster speed than usual.
Brake later than you would without a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride at a slower speed than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight. Your motorcycle will need more time to speed up, slow down, and turn. Ride slower, start slowing earlier, increase your following distance, and look for larger gaps when crossing or merging.

questions.question: When should you use the front brake?

options.text: Every time you slow down or stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you slow down or stop
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does reflective material on your helmet do?

options.text: Should only be used at night
Does not help you be seen

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes you easier to see
questions.explanation: Reflective material on a vest or helmet makes you more visible to other drivers. Use it both day and night.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider stop other drivers from sharing the lane?

options.text: By giving other drivers dirty looks
By riding in the center of the lane
By riding on the left side of the lane
By riding in a zigzag pattern

questions.correctAnswerText: By riding in the center of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane. This leaves less space on either side of your motorcycle and discourages other drivers from sharing the lane.

questions.question: How do you lean a motorcycle for a turn?

options.text: Press the handgrip toward the direction of the turn
Press the handgrip away from the direction of the turn

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip toward the direction of the turn
questions.explanation: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn. This makes the motorcycle lean and turn.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Help you see and be seen
Help you avoid hazards on the road
Invite other drivers into your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers into your lane
questions.explanation: Choose your lane position to stay out of blind spots, increase visibility, avoid hazards, and provide escape routes. Position yourself to discourage other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.question: Which is NOT a safe way to prevent fatigue while riding?

options.text: Protecting yourself from wind, cold, and rain
Limiting how far you ride in one day

questions.correctAnswerText: Taking artificial stimulants
questions.explanation: Take frequent breaks and do not ride more than six hours in one day. Dress to protect yourself from the elements. Do not use artificial stimulants. When they wear off, they can be very dangerous.

questions.question: When you mix alcohol and drugs, the effects are:

options.text: More dangerous than when used separately
Less dangerous than when used separately

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous than when used separately
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medications, impair your riding ability. Some drugs become even more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: Passing on a motorcycle is similar to a car, but:

options.text: Being seen is more important on a motorcycle
Being seen is less important on a motorcycle
Pass on the shoulder, not the main road
Make eye contact with the other driver

questions.correctAnswerText: Being seen is more important on a motorcycle
questions.explanation: The basic passing techniques are the same as in a car. However, visibility is more important for motorcycles because they are smaller and can hide in blind spots or be overlooked by other drivers.

questions.question: What is the best group formation when riding in curves, turning, or entering a highway?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation on straight roads. But when going through curves, turns, or entering or leaving highways, riders should ride in a single-file line.

questions.question: What should you focus on when adjusting your mirrors?

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
The road in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and the lane next to you. You may see the edge of your arm or shoulder, but the road behind and to the side is what matters most.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Protect your lane from other drivers.
Allow you a nice view of scenery.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Hide your intentions from other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your lane from other drivers.
questions.explanation: Good lane position keeps you safe by keeping you out of blind spots, helping you see and be seen, avoiding road hazards, avoiding wind from other vehicles, and giving you an escape route. Position yourself so other drivers will not try to share your lane.

questions.question: What should you do to be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride as closely as possible to the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Riding with your headlight on is the most important thing you can do to help others see you at an intersection. Always keep your headlight on when your motorcycle is running.

questions.question: What should you do if another vehicle is following you too closely?

options.text: Allow the other driver to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the other driver to pass you.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them ahead of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make it worse by encouraging them to tailgate at higher speeds.
